extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: women in the highest quartile of BCAAs had lower odds of breast cancer
extraction_supporting_text.p_value: Computed from the reported effect and 95% CI using a normal approximation: p=2.930e-04.
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: Breast cancer was diagnosed by physical examination, mammography and pathological confirmation.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: The total intake of valine, leucine, and isoleucine from all food items in the questionnaire was used to calculate BCAAs intake.

headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger’s test is generally not recommended when fewer than 10 studies are available.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 4 studies yielded an effect size of 0.98 (95% CI: 0.87–1.11), indicating no statistically significant association between BCAAs and breast cancer. Although the point estimate suggests a potential inverse relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by very high heterogeneity (I² = 79.49%), reflecting highly inconsistent results across studies.
